This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86cf7ceff67c43948f801621b387f5c588857aba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d7dcf16e613f418f4a07615627636c224750ffb` — the merge of head `b6b54ce24488c5516ba008695300343e1beb8e6b` into base `86cf7ceff67c43948f801621b387f5c588857aba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 6d7dcf16e613f418f4a07615627636c224750ffb && git checkout 6d7dcf16e613f418f4a07615627636c224750ffb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 86cf7ceff67c43948f801621b387f5c588857aba b6b54ce24488c5516ba008695300343e1beb8e6b && git checkout -B drift-repro 86cf7ceff67c43948f801621b387f5c588857aba && git merge --no-ff b6b54ce24488c5516ba008695300343e1beb8e6b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86cf7ceff67c43948f801621b387f5c588857aba
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6b54ce24488c5516ba008695300343e1beb8e6b`

Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/preview-undeclared-dimension-parity.test.ts, .changeset/28201-preview-undeclared-dimension.md + packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts `ensureCube` / `query()` / `callCtx` (live gate order, read, not changed), packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts (untouched, read), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/DatasetPreview.tsx, packages/client/src/index.ts (`queryDataset`)

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial on PR body and changeset, arms match). No governed path in the 3-file list; no published schema touched. Base `86cf7cef` already carries #28210.
- (1) Parity: the preview now calls the same private `assertDimensionFields` the live `ensureCube` calls, on the minted cube with `Object.keys(compiled.cube.dimensions)` as the vocabulary, as the live augmented branch does. The refusal is that method's own: `INVALID_FIELD` / 400, `param: 'dimensions'` (or `timeDimensions`), `field`, `object`, `dimension`, "Valid dimensions: …". The test pins `bogus` alone and beside `region`, message byte-equal across native / ObjectQL / preview. Declared `region` and the field-named `amount` serve the same groups on all three faces (CONTROL cells); the gate's own rule ("any of the object's OWN fields may also be used") is unchanged, so a dimension naming a real field is still legal everywhere.
- (2) Order: live is `ensureCube` (measure-fields → dimension-fields → `#20807` scalar-columns → field-type → currency → where-fields) then `query()` (`#21156` caller-members → `callCtx`: body → internal → field-read). The preview now runs measure-fields → dimension-fields → field-type → currency → caller-measures → body → internal → field-read: the same relative order on every pair it asks. It still does not ask `#20807` (`assertDimensionsGroupScalarColumns`) or `assertWhereFields` (the latter is #28257's seam). Single-mistake queries: the four reordered gates refuse disjoint conditions (a non-column-reference spelling cannot resolve to a typed field or a record-currency amount), so no single-mistake answer moves; only the two-mistake cases change, both pinned (`region_sum` + `bogus` → dimension 400; `amount + 1` + `region_sum` → field-type 400) and each with its own ablation arm. This closes the #28210 non-blocking note.
- (3) Clause-② re-derived: one source file, no new function, export, answer member, status or code; `assertDimensionFields` is an existing private method. `no (narrowing)` holds.
- (5) Clients: `ui` `DatasetPreview.tsx` sends the draft dataset's own declared dimension and measure names; dashboard / chart / report renderers name declared dataset members; `packages/client` passes `previewDrafts` through. Nothing relies on the preview serving an undeclared dimension as a `null` group (`git grep previewDrafts` over ui/, packages/client, content/docs, skills).
- (6) Out of scope and filed: `runtimeFilter` on a field the object does not have (#28257, with the unmeasured `#20807` door noted there); dotted `<dataset>.bogus`, which the two live faces refuse differently and needs a ruling (#28258). Correctly left out.
- `preview-evaluator.ts` untouched: an undeclared dimension over a real field is legal there, and the service gate is the judge, as live.
- Check-runs at head: 7 success, 13 skipped, 17 in progress at review time (Build Core, Test Core shards planning, Lint, Type Check, Check Changeset). Dev reports the package suite (199 files, 0 failed), typecheck, lint, all dispatch-gate families and the dogfood battery green at this head.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/service-analytics`: `patch` with BREAKING banner, `!` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — per AGENTS.md a non-protocol narrowing ships patch and keeps its banner and disposition. The changeset body carries Before / Now / Gate order / remedy, no FROM → TO code rewrite; the gate's run is in the pending CI.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Accept-set narrowing on one face only: `queryDataset` with `previewDrafts: true` over a pending seed draft; the refusal is the live faces' existing `INVALID_FIELD` / 400.
- Gate-order change on the same face: which of two mistakes is named first now matches live; no new refusal and no single-mistake change.
- Live native / ObjectQL / `generateSql` paths: unchanged.
- Out of scope, filed: #28257 (where/runtimeFilter unknown field, `#20807`), #28258 (dotted dimension ruling).

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing makes the published contract's own refusal real on the preview: a Studio author sees the dimension typo's refusal before publishing, with the same text. Judging on the minted cube with the compiled vocabulary mirrors the live augmented branch exactly, so the suggestion list cannot offer the typo back.
- Aligning the preview's gate list to live order, with both two-mistake cases pinned and ablated, is the right remedy for the #28210 note; the preview now asks every live door it has the inputs for, in live order, and the two it does not ask are carded rather than silently skipped.
